books.section: Topic 8.2 The Cold War from 1945 to 1980
Truman and the Beginning of the Cold War (1945-1953)

stimulus.source_note: Original summary passage written for this question; facts from the grounding books.
stimulus.text: In June 1948, the Soviet Union closed all roads and railways into West Berlin, a city deep inside the Soviet zone of Germany. The Western Allies answered by flying food, coal, and supplies into the city for nearly a year, landing a plane every few minutes at the height of the effort. In May 1949 the Soviets lifted the blockade, and within months the Western zones became the Federal Republic of Germany and the Soviet zone became the German Democratic Republic.

source: original; stimulus is an original summary passage written for this question
stem: The Soviet blockade of Berlin most directly responded to which Western action?

options.text: The Western plan to merge its zones and issue a new West German currency.
The creation of the Warsaw Pact by the Soviet Union and its allies.
options.misconception: The Warsaw Pact came in 1955; the blockade came in 1948, so the order is backwards.

options.text: The American decision to withdraw its troops from Korea.
options.misconception: Korea is a different place and a later war; it does not explain Berlin in 1948.

options.text: The signing of the SALT I treaty between the superpowers.
options.misconception: SALT I came in 1972, decades after the Berlin blockade.

rationales.A: The Western Allies were merging their zones into a West German state with a new mark, which Moscow read as a permanent division of Germany. Background from the books: the blockade was Stalin's answer to that step, an attempt to force the West to back down.
rationales.B: The Warsaw Pact was created in 1955, seven years after the blockade. A later alliance cannot explain an earlier crisis.
rationales.C: No American withdrawal from Korea explains a blockade in Berlin in 1948 — the Korean War began two years later, in 1950.
rationales.D: SALT I was signed in 1972, more than twenty years after the blockade. It cannot explain an event from 1948.
rationales.general:
1. The blockade began in June 1948, so its cause must be something happening just before that date.
2. Background from the books: Just before it, the Western Allies moved to merge their zones and issue a new currency for West Germany.
3. Moscow read that step as a permanent division of Germany and answered by squeezing Berlin.
Remember: Match the date first: a cause must come before its effect, and close before it counts.
